item.title: Free weekly running sessions offered at Wisbech Park
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Free weekly running sessions offered at Wisbech Park
Residents across the Fens are being invited to join a free, weekly running programme at Wisbech Park. Organised by Active Fenland, the Couch to 5k sessions take place every Tuesday morning between 9:30am and 10:30am.
The group is led by England Athletics-qualified coach Gary Bligh and is open to all abilities, regardless of previous running experience. Organisers say the sessions focus on building confidence and stamina in a supportive environment, with no pressure to meet specific pace targets. Beyond the physical exercise, the group offers a social opportunity for participants to meet new people. Those interested in taking part can simply turn up to the park to get involved.

item.title: Battle of Britain commemoration service in King’s Lynn
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Battle of Britain commemoration service in King’s Lynn
A wreath-laying ceremony will be held in King’s Lynn’s Tower Gardens this Monday to mark the 86th anniversary of the Battle of Britain. The service begins at 10:45am and will be led by the Reverend Canon Mark Dimond. West Norfolk Mayor, Councillor Steve Bearshaw, is expected to attend alongside representatives from the Armed Forces, local schools, and cadet groups.
The event also signals the launch of the Royal Air Forces Association’s annual Wings Appeal. Organisers are encouraging veterans and members of the public to attend the commemoration. Following the service, guests are invited to Marriotts Warehouse for refreshments.

item.title: Metrion Biosciences staff cycle 112 miles for youth charity
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Metrion Biosciences staff cycle 112 miles for youth charity
Staff from the Cambridgeshire-based firm Metrion Biosciences are undertaking a 112-mile cycling challenge today to raise funds for the charity Centre 33. The team is visiting all five of the charity’s hubs, including the site in Wisbech, as well as locations in Peterborough, Huntingdon, and Ely. The ride aims to support the organisation’s work providing mental health and practical assistance to young people aged 13 to 25. Colleagues are also contributing to the fundraising effort by using static bikes at the company's offices. Last year, Centre 33 provided support to nearly 4,000 young people across the region.

item.title: Repairs underway following burst water main in King’s Lynn
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Repairs underway following burst water main in King’s Lynn
A burst water main continues to cause flooding at the Tuesday Market Place in King’s Lynn today. The leak, which was first reported yesterday morning, has resulted in standing water across the town centre, with motorists seen driving through the affected area.
Anglian Water crews are currently on site working to resolve the issue. The utility company expects the repairs to be completed by 1pm today. Local councillor Rob Colwell has described the incident as frustrating for residents who are being asked to conserve water during the current drought. While West Norfolk Council has confirmed that local facilities remain open, commuters are advised to take care when travelling through the town centre.

The hospital is set to discuss its future at an annual members’ meeting this Thursday, which is open to the public.

item.title: Historic Fenland venues open doors for Heritage Open Days
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Historic Fenland venues open doors for Heritage Open Days
Residents across the Fens are invited to explore local history as part of the annual National Heritage Open Days. Over the next two weekends, various sites in Wisbech and March will offer free public access and guided tours.
In March, visitors can view the railway station heritage room or the Masonic Centre. Wisbech venues participating include Peckover House, the Town Hall, and the Fenland Museum. Other highlights include tours of the Tydd Pumping Station, the General Cemetery, and the St Peter and St Paul Church. Opening times and dates vary by location, with events running across September 12, 13, 19, and 20. Full details on specific opening hours for each venue are available through local listings.
